clue.text: Remained restrained

definitions.meaning: to have ... somewhere is to have stayed there, as in stopping at a friend's house

explanation.surface: Someone stayed put because they were held back.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are everyday British usage: 'stop' for stay a while, and 'stop' for hold back or prevent.

clue.text: Love is casual, loose, and lustful

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Casual love is lascivious.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewd and lecherous, full of sexual desire.

clue.text: Thrust forward, and died loyal, capturing 500

explanation.surface: A loyal soldier died charging forward while capturing 500 prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: To push oneself or something forward unwelcomely is to intrude.

clue.text: Churchmen in divorce? You could write on it!

clue.text: In adversity, drink

definitions.meaning: ... on one's luck, in a bad way
to swallow a drink in one go

explanation.surface: Someone in hard times turns to the bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Being down means having a bad time; to down a pint is to swallow it quickly.

clue.text: Bravo, perhaps, gets one bill after another

explanation.surface: Someone receives one invoice after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bravo' looks like a name or the radio code word; it is a shout of praise, given as an example, hence 'perhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting bravo is an example of loud public praise.

clue.text: Soured about one getting flattered all round

explanation.surface: A man flattered on every side turns sour.
explanation.walkthrough: CI goes after the first A of ADULATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Made slightly acid or sharp in taste.

clue.text: Completely cold and unproductive

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
lean years are unproductive ones

explanation.surface: A thoroughly cold and barren place.
explanation.definitionFit: To get clean away is to escape entirely.

clue.text: Eager to appear in one Scottish mystical interpretation

indicators.note: the word for eager shows up inside the Scots word

parts.note: ane is the Scots word for one
agog means eager or excited

clue.text: Paid — about to put up a musical work

indicators.note: the word for paid goes about the turned word

parts.note: to meet a bill is to pay it

parts.note: taken as written

clue.text: Dead right? Not now

parts.note: the late Mr Smith is the dead Mr Smith

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether 'dead right' is correct and is told to wait.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done not at present but afterwards is done subsequently.

clue.text: Innocent allurement of small fry

parts.note: white is the colour of purity and innocence
bait is anything used to lure or tempt

explanation.surface: Tiny fish tempted by an innocent-looking lure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small fry' is read literally: the young of herring and sprats, eaten fried whole in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Young fish are called fry, and these are tiny ones caught and eaten whole.

clue.text: Was in time for about anything

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about with dates
aught is an old word for anything at all

explanation.surface: Someone arrived punctually for whatever was going.

clue.text: Act to cover the renegade

clue.text: One way and another, bad. Stop!

another way, another ST
ill means bad, as in ill will

explanation.surface: Things are bad both ways, so a halt is called.
explanation.definitionFit: A complete halt in which nothing moves.

clue.text: To be seen in some part like Falstaff

explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Falstaff is famous for his huge girth, so like him means very fat.

clue.text: Passing, sees Ian's in trouble in the river

clue.text: Astounded — not all at the same time

definitions.meaning: arranged in turns, as with working hours

explanation.definitionFit: Being dumbfounded is being knocked sideways; shifts or starts spread over time are also described with this word.

clue.text: Sweet girl, well-adjusted all round, went underground

clue.text: Real meaning of wealth

definitions.meaning: the gist or essential content of something
a man of means and property, as in a person of some standing

explanation.surface: A question about what wealth truly signifies.

clue.text: Part one bird from another

clue.text: At full speed in a German river

parts.note: the Main flows through Frankfurt to the Rhine

explanation.surface: Something races along a river in Germany.

clue.text: Nemesis, unfortunately, takes a high place

clue.text: Apocryphal Jew gets 12½ cents to start with

clue.text: Proportion not all share

clue.text: Gun in a mess — work round with Chinese varnish
